_about: Step 4d (decision 40, rule G27, the orchestrator's 5 Oct addition): Cook's words and lines as the language engine's own source. They used to live in data/cook.json (words: the Kutchi, English, gender, forms and voice spellings; lines; grammar; the guide box's English; the pantry headline) and data/stations/*.json (the station words, the stir line); build/lang/import_cook.mjs reads them from here, and the game reads none of it (js/cook/words.js asks the engine). Edit a word here, or better in the engine's hand/ layer, then run node build/lang/import_all.mjs. data/cook.json keeps only the item catalogue (pictures, heaps, layers) under the same ids. The parked pages (dress, find, snap, tidy, monsoon) still read this file through js/cook/lang.js, their adapter, until they move onto the engine.

grammar._about: How this language builds sentences. The code only names roles (an order's first line, a list, a counted noun); the words are in `words` and the frames in `lines`. Another language (Gujarati first) swaps this block with those two. Order ladder: `order` frames start each dish, `list.next` joins things in any order, `then` (the line key) joins the next step of a sequence ("Ne poi {x}.", a draft from Zafar, Mum to confirm), `no` says leave-it-out rows ("{x} na.", Mum 26 Sept, B1: two words, like `and`, so a hidden no-row isn't given away by its shape), and `then_word` is the linker's word id: from its word stage 3 the ladder stops drawing the sequence and only the spoken linker tells you the order.

order._polite: 28 Sept (Zafar): an order's first line is short at level 1 (Muke chai khape.) and polite from level 2 (Tu muke chai banai dinda?, Mum's B40 frame; both recorded for chai)

gender._about: Words agree with a noun's gender (words[id].gender: he | she | unknown). A word with `forms` ({he, she}) takes the form for the noun it goes with: "one" (hakro/hakri) and describing words (wadho/wadhi). Unknown gender (most nouns until the family says) takes the word's own `kutchi`; the order frame Muke {x} khape is the informal one and never changes (docs/language/grammar-notes.md 1).
